I'll search for information on how to type up meeting minutes effectively.

<tool>web_search</tool>
<query>how to type meeting minutes format template best practices</query>

Based on my search, here's a comprehensive guide on how to type up minutes of a meeting:

## Before the Meeting

- **Review the agenda** and any previous minutes to understand the meeting's purpose
- **Prepare a template** with the basic structure already in place
- **Bring or have ready**: attendee list, agenda, previous action items, and a recording device (if permitted)

## During the Meeting

- **Record key information**: date, time, location, attendees, and those absent
- **Note the meeting type** (regular, special, annual, etc.)
- **Document decisions made**, not every word spoken
- **Track action items**: who is responsible and deadlines
- **Note motions** and voting results (for formal meetings)
- **Record points of order** or procedural matters

## Standard Format for Typed Minutes

### Header
- Organization name
- Meeting type and date
- Time started and ended
- Location (physical or virtual)
- Attendees (present and absent)

### Body
- **Call to order** – who called it and at what time
- **Approval of previous minutes** – note any corrections
- **Reports** – summaries of officer/committee reports (not verbatim)
- **Old business** – follow-up on previous items
- **New business** – new topics discussed and decisions
- **Announcements**
- **Adjournment** – time and who moved it

### Action Items Table (often separate)
| Action Item | Responsible Person | Deadline | Status |

## Writing Tips

- Use **past tense** and **third person** ("The chair stated..." not "I think...")
- Be **concise and objective** – minutes are factual records, not transcripts
- Use **clear, simple language**
- **Avoid opinions, debates, or detailed discussions** – record conclusions only
- Use **standard naming** for people after first mention
- Proofread carefully before distribution

## After the Meeting

- **Type up promptly** while memory is fresh (ideally within 24 hours)
- **Review against your notes** and any recording
- **Submit to the chair/secretary** for approval
- **Distribute to attendees** and relevant stakeholders
- **File securely** for future reference and legal compliance

## Tools to Consider

- Microsoft Word or Google Docs templates
- Dedicated meeting minutes software (Minutes.io, Fellow, Notion)
- Project management tools with meeting features (Asana, Monday.com)

Would you like more specific guidance for a particular type of meeting (board meeting, team standup, committee meeting, etc.)?
